reproducibility: Bit-for-bit reproducible from source: the same CI run built every image twice more from two clean checkouts in two different directories, with no shared cache, and got identical digests (job "Reproducible boot images"); the BIOS image is also byte-identical to the one an earlier, independent run built. image-builder removes the two sources of non-determinism found along the way — random GPT GUIDs, and the link time and CodeView GUID the linker stamps into the embedded UEFI loader. A Windows host builds different bytes, because Rust embeds the build host's source paths in panic locations; the published files are the Linux CI build.
notice: Release candidate note: the UEFI image first uploaded here (SHA-256 eb7d566c7fcafd9a4ee672b0ede9b3c3456b9577b799698fd982d2ff72c45571) was replaced before v0.8.1 was tagged, because a clean rebuild did not reproduce it (it carried its loader's link time). The BIOS image did not change. If you downloaded that UEFI file, it boots the same system, but it is not the release and cannot be reproduced.
